speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are presenting with wrist pain and difficulty moving your hand. To begin our evaluation, can you tell me exactly where the pain is located and when it started?

speaker: Patient
text: 34-year-old female. The patient reports experiencing pain in her right thumb and wrist, which radiates to her elbow for the past three months. The pain worsens when she holds her infant son and is alleviated somewhat with an ice pack. She mentions a history of falling on her right outstretched hand about six months ago. She also notes that her mother has a history of chronic joint pain treated with methotrexate. The patient has been taking ibuprofen as needed for her symptoms.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Carpal Tunnel Syndrome. The patient's symptoms of right thumb and wrist pain radiating to the elbow, exacerbated by gripping an infant and relieved by ice, along with a family history of autoimmune arthritis, are classic for CTS. While the fall six months ago could suggest a fracture or ligament injury, the chronic nature and specific aggravating factors point strongly to nerve compression. I recommend an ultrasound or MRI of the wrist to confirm the diagnosis and rule out other causes like a fracture or ganglion cyst. REQUEST IMAGES: Wrist_ultrasound
